title: Add Fly.io deployment recipe aligned with quickstart template conventions
author: Sabrina James
release_notes: New Fly.io deployment recipe for the RAG+agents example, including secrets/env var guidance and OTel-friendly defaults.
body:
Summary: Adds a Fly.io deployment recipe for the RAG + agents example app that matches the quickstart template conventions (env var schema, secret handling, health checks, and observability defaults). This is intended as a copy/pasteable path from local dev to a real internet-facing deployment without introducing insecure defaults.

Motivation: Solutions Engineering and early internal beta testers asked for a “single-node, real deployment” option that is simpler than k8s but still production-minded. Fly.io is a good fit for the PLG persona and for quick demos, and the recipe reinforces template patterns (REDWOOD_* env vars, timeouts/retries, and OTel wiring).

What’s included: 1) A new docs page under examples/deploy describing prerequisites, setup, deploy, and troubleshooting. 2) A fly.toml and Dockerfile pattern that uses the same port/config conventions as the templates. 3) Explicit notes on secrets vs config env vars (fly secrets set vs fly deploy --env). 4) OTel notes: how to point OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT at a collector, and what to do if you don’t have one (logs still include request_id/correlation_id).

Security/PII notes: The recipe avoids putting API keys in fly.toml. It also calls out log redaction expectations and warns against exporting full prompts/tool payloads to logs. The docs include a small section on turning on template adoption telemetry tags only if your network/proxy policy allows it.

Operator notes: Uses a simple /healthz endpoint for Fly checks and recommends setting a conservative concurrency to reduce 429s for self-serve accounts. Includes guidance on setting REDWOOD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS and max token caps via env.

Testing: Verified locally with flyctl deploy on a test org and exercised streaming responses end-to-end. CI runs lint + docs link checks.

Follow-ups (not in scope): adding a “doctor” command integration specific to Fly deployments, and shipping a managed OTel collector setup for Fly.
commits: docs(deploy): add Fly.io deployment guide for rag-agent example
chore(flyio): add fly.toml template and health check notes
chore(docker): align example container port and startup command with templates
docs(security): clarify secrets vs env vars and telemetry opt-in
review_conversation:
Dana Lo: Can we make it explicit that REDWOOD_API_KEY must be a Fly secret and not an env var in fly.toml? Also please mirror the template env var names exactly (REDWOOD_MODEL, REDWOOD_BASE_URL, OTEL_*).

Sabrina James: Updated the guide to use `fly secrets set REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` as the only recommended path, and added a callout box + grep-able warning in README. Also aligned the env var names with the template config schema.

Allison Grant: On the OTel section: please avoid high-cardinality attributes in the example logs (don’t suggest logging full prompt/tool args). Also can we add a minimal example that works without a collector?

Sabrina James: Removed the prompt/tool payload logging snippet and replaced with request_id + route + model + status + latency fields. Added a “no collector” path: logs-only still works, and tracing can be enabled later by setting OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT + OTEL_SERVICE_NAME.

Christine Wong: Health checks: Fly will restart aggressively if /healthz depends on upstream calls. Make sure it’s purely local. Also recommend a conservative concurrency setting and mention 429 mitigation.

Sabrina James: Confirmed /healthz returns local process readiness only (no Redwood calls). Added a recommended `services.concurrency` block and a troubleshooting entry for 429s with backoff + reduced concurrency.

Elliot Price: Docs style: please follow the standardized quickstart headings (Prereqs / Configure / Deploy / Verify / Troubleshoot). Also add a short snippet for `fly logs` and where to look for request IDs.

Sabrina James: Restructured the page to match the template README format and added log commands + request_id guidance.
merge_outcome: Merged into main; recipe published with docs link from deploy index.
notes: Telemetry tagging is documented as opt-in due to some corporate proxies rejecting unknown headers; guidance points to disabling template-origin tags if users see unexpected 4xx from intermediaries.
